subject: Post-call: inference cost snapshot & next steps
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Anita Shah <anita@clearleaf.ai>, Tom Reynolds <tom.reynolds@clearleaf.ai>
Cc: laura.bennett@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 02 Apr 2027 15:20:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call: inference cost snapshot & next steps

Hi Anita / Tom — thanks again for the 30-minute sync today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we’re aligned.

Summary of what you shared (pain points):
- Token/unit economics: customer-facing features (autocomplete + summarization) are growing quickly; current cost per 1k tokens is variable and spikes on peak usage, making unit economics unstable.
- Throughput & tail latency: occasional 95th/99th spikes hurting UX during traffic bursts.
- Engineering ops: currently running on GCP preemptible VMs with a homegrown batching layer; autoscaling is manual and fragile.

Current stack you mentioned:
- Serving: self-hosted OpenModel v1.2 (FP16) on GCP preemptible A100s
- Orchestration: K8s + custom autoscaler, Redis for cache (not currently used for KV cache across sessions)
- Observability: basic Prometheus + Grafana, no token-level cost breakdowns yet

Success criteria you called out:
- Reduce per-token inference cost by ~2.5-3x (target: ~33% of current cost) without degrading quality beyond a small, measurable threshold
- 95th latency < 300ms for interactive features, P90 < 150ms where possible
- Predictable monthly spend (smoother tails) and a clear roll-to-prod path for pilot to 2–3 services

Openness to technical approaches you confirmed:
- Quantization: open to trying int8 and 4-bit quantized variants if quality holds for core prompts
- Batching/caching: willing to enable prefix and KV caching for chat flows; want to understand impact on latency for short conversational turns

Proposed next steps (what we’ll do from Redwood):
1) Share a short workload template (attached) — you provide a sample of typical prompt lengths, concurrency distribution, and traffic window for a 24-hour busy period.
2) We’ll run an offline econ estimate + model variant suggestions (int8, 4-bit candidates) and return a 2-page estimate PDF by Wednesday.
3) Scope a 2-week pilot: measure unit cost, quality metrics on your eval prompts, and latency SLOs. We’ll propose a canary rollout plan for one service.
4) If procurement is involved, introduce commercial/terms contacts — we can provide an initial pricing estimate and a draft SOW.

Attachments: redwood_pricing_estimate_v1.pdf (high-level estimate), clearleaf_action_items.xlsx (workload template + action items)

Would appreciate confirmation on:
- Which service(s) you want in the pilot (autocomplete, nightly-summarization, or both)
- Who on your side will own sample dataset delivery and procurement coordination
- Any blackout dates for a pilot in April

Thanks — I’ll queue the workload template and a short questionnaire.

Jordan Blake
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
jordan.blake@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0164
Redwood Inference

---

> 
> > Anita
From: Anita Shah <anita@clearleaf.ai>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 02 Apr 2027 18:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: inference cost snapshot & next steps

Jordan — this is a helpful summary, thank you. A few quick clarifications from our side: 
- Priority: 1) Cost, 2) latency for autocomplete, 3) preservation of generation quality for customer-facing replies.
- Pilot scope: we’d like to start with autocomplete only (high QPS, short prompts) — if that goes well, we’ll add summarization.
- Data/sample owner: Tom will send the sample workload and a small eval set. He’s cc’d here.
- Quantization: we are willing to try aggressive quantization on non-critical prompts, but we’ll validate on the eval set before broader rollout.

Timeline: if you can share the initial estimate by next Wed ET, we can review and aim to start a pilot mid-April.

Also — procurement: I’ll loop them in if the estimate looks reasonable.

Best,
Anita
Head of Product, ClearLeaf Analytics
anita@clearleaf.ai

Jordan / Anita — thanks. Procurement here — two quick asks from our side to keep timelines moving: 
1) We’ll need a ballpark monthly commitment estimate and a draft SOW / MSA early in the pilot conversation so our legal can pre-review. A not-to-exceed pilot price works for us initially.
2) Please include a short bullet on data handling: where logs/requests are stored during pilot and retention window. We operate under standard privacy controls and must confirm no PII is retained beyond 30 days unless agreed.

If you can send an initial pricing stub and the draft SOW link, we’ll queue internal approval.

Thanks,

Laura — forwarding the thread. Key asks from ClearLeaf: mid-April pilot on autocomplete, Tom needs draft SOW + data handling bullets, Anita wants 1–2 day turn on the estimate.

My proposed internal plan:
- Action A: I’ll finalize the 2-page econ estimate and attach the pricing stub (deliverable Wed).
- Action B: Solutions/infra should prepare a short tech note on quantization impact (int8 vs 4-bit) for short prompts — include likely latency and memory uplift, and suggested model variants.
- Action C: Legal/commercial: prepare a pilot SOW template and a standard 30-day data retention clause.

Also thinking we offer a one-time pilot credit (30% off inference charges during the 2-week pilot) to accelerate evaluation — ok to propose that?

Jordan Blake
